# Naming the expense split of a cash purchase as a bill's settlement.
#
# The account-type refusal on the bill side. `Expenses:Supplies:USD` holds
# dollars, so the commodity check has nothing to say and it is the account
# arm of the message that fires — the arm that names the record's own
# account, which for a bill is the **payable**.
#
# The cost is not money waiting to be identified: it is the purchase. Moving
# it onto the payable would take the expense out of the P&L and leave a bill
# reading paid by nothing, with every figure still balancing.
#
# What this fixture produces: a refusal naming the expense account and the
# payable, with the cost still on it.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
bill "BILL-USD-001"
  vendor_id: "V-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Parts"
    account: "Expenses:Supplies"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ap_account: "Liabilities:Accounts Payable USD"
    memo: "Bill BILL-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-03-26
    amount: 100
    account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
    txn_guid: "7f8a9b0c5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e"
    txn_split_guid: "9b0c5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a"
